locator.section: 8 / Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Random or hidden rearrangements)

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.7, row 1 -> row 2 (arrow labelled 'low energy'). Same beta-cleavage bond changes as the high-energy channel, but the two fragments do NOT separate: the book draws them inside square brackets as a non-covalent ion-molecule complex [1-butene ... CH2=CH-OH+.]. A complex is not a single mapped SMILES, so it is encoded here as the two-species product state {enol radical cation, 1-butene}; they remain associated (held by ion-dipole forces, per the page's text about threshold-energy fragments being trapped in a potential well) and go on to exchange hydrogen (steps IMS8-EQ8.7d, IMS8-EQ8.7e) rather than dissociating. Book draws 0 arc(s) on the 'low energy' arrow itself; the 5 moves are the implicit beta-cleavage flow, identical to IMS8-EQ8.7b. The curved arrows drawn INSIDE the bracket belong to the following intra-complex H-transfer step (IMS8-EQ8.7d), not to this cleavage.

Cross-link: MØD rule IMS_8_7_3 (rule_name 'Hydrogen exchange occring in a Ion-Molecule-Complex 8.7 row 2 low energy'). Its DFS is IDENTICAL to IMS_8_7_2: [C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C]6([H]7){=}[O+]8[H]9 >> [C]1[C]2[C]3{=}[C]4.[C]5{=}[C]6([H]7)[O+.]8[H]9. VERIFIED consistent with this record's bond/charge/spin change. The MØD rule emits the two separated fragments; the book's low-energy distinction (fragments retained as an ion-molecule complex, then H-exchanging) is not representable in a single MØD term-graph rule and is captured here at the mechanism-record level via the following two steps.
